title: Feelings & support
goal: Notice when a friend is down and comfort them, say sorry and mean it, congratulate someone properly and offer condolences the Sindhi way.
intro:
Friendships are made in the moments when something goes wrong — or very right. This unit gives you what people in Sindh really say when a friend is stressed (**ڳڻتي نه ڪر، يار**), hurt (**اها ڳالهه دل تي نه وٺ**), grieving (**الله توهان کي صبر ڏئي**) or celebrating (**مبارڪون هجن!**).

On the grammar side you'll see how Sindhi lets feelings *happen to* you (**مون کي کل اچي وئي** 'I burst out laughing'), how to say *as soon as*, *while* and *until*, and the very Sindhi way of owning up to a mistake without sounding as if you planned it: **مون کان غلطي ٿي وئي**.

grammar.title: Feelings that happen to you: مون کي ڏک ٿيو، مون کي کل آئي
grammar.body:
In unit 14 you met **مون کي ڪاوڙ آئي** 'I got angry'. Sindhi treats many feelings not as something *you* do but as something that **happens to you**. The person who feels takes **کي** (مون کي، تو کي، هن کي، اسان کي، توهان کي), the feeling is the grammatical subject, and the verb agrees with the **feeling**, not with you.

Three verbs do most of the work:

**اچڻ** 'come' — a feeling that wells up: **کل** اچڻ 'to laugh', **ڪاوڙ** اچڻ 'to get angry', **X جي ياد** اچڻ 'to miss X'.
**لڳڻ** 'strike, seem' — an impression: **خراب** لڳڻ 'to feel hurt / bad', **سٺو** لڳڻ 'to feel nice', **ڊپ** لڳڻ 'to be scared'.
**ٿيڻ** 'happen' — an emotion that occurs: **ڏک** ٿيڻ 'to feel sad', **خوشي** ٿيڻ 'to be glad', **ساڙ** ٿيڻ 'to be jealous', **ڳڻتي** or **ٽينشن** ٿيڻ 'to get worried / stressed'.

For a feeling that comes **suddenly**, add وڃڻ: مون کي کل **اچي وئي** 'I burst out laughing'. For one going on right now, use **پيو / پئي**: مون کي گهر جي ياد **پئي اچي** 'I'm missing home'. For something that always happens, use the habitual: امتحان کان اڳ مون کي ٽينشن **ٿيندي آهي**.

What caused it often comes first as a 'hearing / seeing' form: اهو **ٻڌي** ڏک ٿيو 'I was sad to hear that'.

**The trap:** never مان ڏک ٿيس or مان خراب لڳس. And watch the agreement — it follows the feeling's gender: ڏک ٿيو (ڏک m), خوشي ٿي (f), کل آئي (f), ساڙ ٿو ٿئي (m), ٽينشن ٿي ٿئي (f).

grammar.title: 'As soon as', 'while' and 'until': -ڻ سان ئي، -ندي، جيستائين
grammar.body:
Three compact patterns link two actions in time.

**As soon as — infinitive + سان ئي**
Put the infinitive in its oblique form (-ṇa) and add **سان ئي** ('with … itself'): گهر **پهچڻ سان ئي** فون ڪجو 'call as soon as you get home'; اهو **ٻڌڻ سان ئي** 'the moment (I) heard it'. Without ئي it still works, just less sharply.

**While — the -ndo participle in -e**
Take the future/participle stem (ڪند-، ڳالهائيند-، هلائيند-) and end it in **-e** (written ي): **ڪندي** kande, **کائيندي** khāīnde, **هلائيندي** halāīnde 'while doing / eating / driving': گاڏي هلائيندي فون نه ڏسو 'don't look at your phone while driving'. Both actions belong to the same person. **Doubled**, it means 'in the middle of, while still …': ڳالهائيندي ڳالهائيندي هوءَ سمهي پئي 'she fell asleep mid-conversation'.

**Until / as long as — جيستائين**
**جيستائين** … (**تيستائين**) … 'as long as … (till then) …': جيستائين مان هتي آهيان، ڳڻتي نه ڪر 'as long as I'm here, don't worry'.
**The trap:** to say *until*, Sindhi puts a **negative** in the جيستائين clause — literally 'as long as X hasn't happened': جيستائين هو معافي **نه** گهرندو، مان هن سان نه ڳالهائيندس 'until he apologises, I won't talk to him'. Leave out that نه and the sentence means the opposite.

With a time or a place, 'until' is simply **تائين** (unit 11): شام **تائين**، گهر **تائين**.

examples.en: Give me a call as soon as you reach the office.

examples.en: As long as I'm here, don't worry.

grammar.title: Owning a mistake: مون کان غلطي ٿي وئي
grammar.body:
Sindhi has two ways to say 'I made a mistake', and the difference is about intention.

**مون غلطي ڪئي** — the ordinary past of ڪرڻ (unit 16; غلطي is f, so ڪئي): *I made a mistake*. Plain and factual.
**مون کان غلطي ٿي وئي** — literally 'a mistake happened **from me**'. The doer takes **کان**, the verb is ٿيڻ (+ وڃڻ), and the sentence says *I did it, but I didn't mean to*. This is the form people use when they apologise.

The same **مون کان + intransitive verb** pattern covers any accident: مون کان تنهنجو فون **ٽٽي ويو** 'I (accidentally) broke your phone', مون کان ڪنجي **گم ٿي وئي** 'I (somehow) lost the key'. In the negative it means *I can't manage it*: **مون کان اهو ڪم نه ٿيندو** 'I can't do that'.

A ladder of apologies, light to heavy:
**سوري / سوري يار** — bumping into someone, being late.
**مون کان غلطي ٿي وئي** — owning up.
**مون کي معاف ڪر / ڪجو** — asking forgiveness for something that hurt.
**مان معافي گهران ٿو / ٿي** — formal: work, elders, messages.

Add **منهنجو اهو مطلب نه هو** 'I didn't mean it like that'. The usual replies: **ڪا ڳالهه ناهي**، **ڇڏ يار** 'forget it', **معاف ڪيو** 'forgiven'.

examples.en: I made a mistake, I admit it. (man)

examples.roman: sorī, moṃ khāṃ tunhinjī kunjī gumu thī vaī.

examples.roman: moṃ khāṃ uho kamu na thīndo.
examples.en: I can't do that. / That's beyond me.

examples.en: OK, forgiven — but don't do it again!

dialogue.title: Bad news at the café
dialogue.setting: Bilawal finds his friend Sanam sitting quietly at their usual café in Qasimabad, Hyderabad, after a bank job she wanted fell through.

lines.speaker: Bilawal
lines.native: سنم! خير ته آهي؟ ڇا ٿيو؟
lines.roman: sanam! xairu ta āhe? chhā thiyo?
lines.en: Sanam! Is everything OK? What happened?

lines.speaker: Sanam
lines.native: ڪجهه به نه… بئنڪ وارن جو جواب آيو. نوڪري نه ملي.
lines.roman: kujhu bi na… bainka vāran jo javābu āyo. nokirī na milī.
lines.en: Nothing… the bank got back to me. I didn't get the job.

lines.speaker: Bilawal
lines.native: اڙي! اهو ٻڌي ڏاڍو ڏک ٿيو. تو ته ڏاڍي محنت ڪئي هئي.
lines.roman: aṛe! uho ɓudhī ɗāḍho ɗukhu thiyo. to ta ɗāḍhī mehnata kaī huī.
lines.en: Oh no! I'm so sorry to hear that. You'd worked so hard.

lines.speaker: Sanam
lines.native: جواب پڙهڻ سان ئي منهنجيون اکيون ڀرجي آيون. آفيس ۾، سڀني جي اڳيان!
lines.roman: javābu paṛhaṇa sāṃ ī munhinjūṃ akhyūṃ bharijī āyūṃ. āfīsa meṃ, sabhinī jī aɠiyāṃ!
lines.en: The moment I read it my eyes filled with tears. In the office, in front of everyone!

lines.speaker: Bilawal
lines.native: ويچاري… اها ڳالهه دل تي نه وٺ. نقصان انهن جو آهي.
lines.roman: vichārī… uhā ɠālhi dila te na vaṭhu. nuqsānu unhan jo āhe.
lines.en: Poor thing… don't take it to heart. It's their loss.

lines.speaker: Sanam
lines.native: ۽ ڪالهه رات تو منهنجو فون به نه کنيو.
lines.roman: ai kālha rāti to munhinjo fon bi na khanyo.
lines.en: And last night you didn't even pick up my call.

lines.speaker: Bilawal
lines.native: سوري، سوري! مون کان غلطي ٿي وئي. فون سائلنٽ تي هو.
lines.roman: sorī, sorī! moṃ khāṃ ġalatī thī vaī. fon sāilanṭa te ho.
lines.en: Sorry, sorry! My fault. The phone was on silent.

lines.speaker: Sanam
lines.native: هون… چڱو، معاف ڪيو. پر اڄ جي چانهه تنهنجي طرفان.
lines.roman: hūṃ… chaṅgo, māf kayo. para aʄu jī chānhi tunhinjī tarafāṃ.
lines.en: Hmm… fine, forgiven. But today's tea is on you.

lines.speaker: Bilawal
lines.native: پڪ! ۽ ٻڌ، جيستائين تو کي سٺي نوڪري نه ٿي ملي، مان روز تنهنجي سي وي چيڪ ڪندس.
lines.roman: paka! ai ɓudhu, jestāīṃ to khe suṭhī nokirī na thī mile, māṃ roz tunhinjī sī vī chek kandus.
lines.en: Deal! And listen, until you get a good job, I'll check your CV every day.

lines.speaker: Sanam
lines.native: روز؟ تون ته پنهنجا ميسيج به نٿو پڙهين!
lines.roman: roz? tūṃ ta panhinjā mesej bi natho paṛheṃ!
lines.en: Every day? You don't even read your own messages!

lines.speaker: Bilawal
lines.native: ڏس! کل اچي وئي نه! حوصلو رک، ٻي نوڪري ضرور تنهنجي هوندي.
lines.roman: ɗisu! khila achī vaī na! hauslo rakhu, ɓī nokirī zarūr tunhinjī hundī.
lines.en: See! You laughed! Chin up — the next job will definitely be yours.

lines.speaker: Sanam
lines.native: مهرباني، بلاول. سچ پچ، تو سان ڳالهائي دل کي سڪون مليو.
lines.roman: meharbānī, bilāval. sach pach, to sāṃ ɠālhāe dila khe sukūnu milyo.
lines.en: Thanks, Bilawal. Honestly, talking to you has made me feel so much better.

lines.speaker: Bilawal
lines.native: مان تو سان گڏ آهيان. ادا، ٻه ڪوپ چانهه ۽ ٻه سموسا!
lines.roman: māṃ to sāṃ gaɗu āhiyāṃ. adā, ɓa kopa chānhi ai ɓa samosā!
lines.en: I'm here for you. Bhai — two cups of tea and two samosas!

culture:
Comfort in Sindh is practical more than wordy. Friends say **ڳڻتي نه ڪر** and then *do* something: order tea, turn up at the door, sit with you. Between close friends a stream of 'thank you's and 'sorry's sounds distant — a quick **سوري يار** or **ڇڏ يار** is enough. With elders and at work, apologise properly (**معاف ڪجو**, **مان معافي گهران ٿو**) and use توهان.

Good news brings an immediate demand: **مٺائي کاراءِ!** 'treat us to sweets!' — passing an exam, a promotion or an engagement means you buy the mithai. Besides **مبارڪون**, you'll hear the warmly Sindhi **واڌايون** (vādhāyūṃ), especially from older people and in villages. Telling a friend **مون کي ساڙ ٿو ٿئي** is a joke and a compliment.

When someone dies, people go to the family's home for **پرسو** — you don't need an invitation. Among Muslims, visitors sit down, raise their hands together for a silent **فاتحه** (prayer for the dead), and then say **الله پاڪ مغفرت ڪري** and **الله توهان کي صبر ڏئي**. Talk is quiet; tea is served; people often keep visiting for three days. Use the respectful plural for the person who has died (**ڏاڏا گذاري ويا**). Hindu Sindhi families have their own rites and say **ڀڳوان سندس آتما کي شانتي ڏي**. On WhatsApp you'll see **انا لله و انا اليه راجعون** or simply 'RIP'.

tip.title: مون کي ڏک ٿيو — feelings happen to you
tip.body:
- The person who feels takes **کي**: مون کي، تو کي، هن کي.
- The feeling is the subject: **ڏک ٿيڻ** 'feel sad', **خراب لڳڻ** 'feel hurt', **کل اچڻ** 'laugh', **ساڙ ٿيڻ** 'be jealous'.
- The verb agrees with the **feeling**: ڏک **ٿيو** (m) · خوشي **ٿي** (f).
- Never مان ڏک ٿيس.
tip.pattern: مون کي + feeling + ٿيڻ / لڳڻ / اچڻ

sentences.native: جڏهن هن اهو چيو، مون کي ڏاڍو خراب لڳو.

sentences.en: When he said that, it really hurt.

sentences.native: اهو ٻڌي ڏاڍو ڏک ٿيو. هاڻي هوءَ ڪيئن آهي؟
sentences.roman: uho ɓudhī ɗāḍho ɗukhu thiyo. hāṇe hūa kīeṃ āhe?
sentences.en: I'm so sorry to hear that. How is she now?

lessons.title: Cheering a friend up

tip.title: Comforting: friend or elder?
tip.body:
- To a friend use the bare stem: ڳڻتي نه **ڪر**، حوصلو **رک**، **گهٻراءِ** نه، **ڊڄ** نه.
- To an elder or stranger use **-o**: ڳڻتي نه **ڪريو**، حوصلو **رکو**، گهٻرايو نه.
- Add **يار** (friend), **ادا / ادي** (brother / sister) or **سائين** to sound warm.

new: اها ڳالهه دل تي نه وٺ.

sentences.native: گهٻراءِ نه، سڀ ٺيڪ ٿيندو.
sentences.roman: ghabrāi na, sabhu ṭhīku thīndo.
sentences.en: Don't panic, everything will be fine. (to a friend)

sentences.native: امان، ڳڻتي نه ڪريو، مان ٺيڪ آهيان.
sentences.roman: amāṃ, ɠaṇatī na karyo, māṃ ṭhīku āhiyāṃ.
sentences.en: Mum, don't worry, I'm fine.

sentences.native: ڊڄ نه، مان تو سان گڏ آهيان.
sentences.roman: ḍaʄu na, māṃ to sāṃ gaɗu āhiyāṃ.
sentences.en: Don't be scared, I'm right here with you.

sentences.native: حوصلو رک، يار. ايندڙ ڀيري ضرور ٿيندو.
sentences.roman: hauslo rakhu, yār. endaṛa bhere zarūr thīndo.
sentences.en: Chin up, mate. Next time it'll definitely work out.

sentences.native: ٿورو صبر ڪريو، سائين، ڊاڪٽر اچي رهيو آهي.
sentences.roman: thoro sabru karyo, sāīṃ, ḍākṭaru achī rahyo āhe.
sentences.en: Please be patient a little, sir, the doctor is on his way.

sentences.native: پاڻ کي سنڀال، يار.
sentences.roman: pāṇa khe sambhālu, yār.
sentences.en: Pull yourself together, mate.

sentences.native: ڳڻتي نه ڪر، يار. مان سڀ سنڀالي وٺندس.
sentences.roman: ɠaṇatī na karu, yār. māṃ sabhu sambhālī vaṭhandus.
sentences.en: Don't worry, mate. I'll handle everything. (man)

sentences.native: ويچارو! هن کي ڏاڍي ٽينشن آهي، هن کي دلاسو ڏي.
sentences.roman: vichāro! hun khe ɗāḍhī ṭenshan āhe, hun khe dilāso ɗe.
sentences.en: Poor guy! He's really stressed — go and comfort him.

sentences.native: اها ڳالهه دل تي نه وٺ، هو مذاق پيو ڪري.
sentences.roman: uhā ɠālhi dila te na vaṭhu, hū mazāqu peyo kare.
sentences.en: Don't take it to heart, he's just joking.

sentences.native: پريشان نه ٿيو، اسين توهان سان گڏ آهيون.
sentences.roman: pareshānu na thiyo, asīṃ tavhāṃ sāṃ gaɗu āhyūṃ.
sentences.en: Don't worry, we're with you. (polite)

tip.title: مون کان غلطي ٿي وئي — it was my fault
tip.body:
- **مون غلطي ڪئي** = I made a mistake (plain fact).
- **مون کان غلطي ٿي وئي** = 'a mistake happened from me' — I did it but didn't mean to. Doer + **کان**, verb ٿيڻ / وڃڻ.
- Accidents too: مون **کان** فون ٽٽي ويو.
- Light to heavy: سوري → مون کي معاف ڪر → معافي گهران ٿو.
tip.pattern: مون کان + thing + ٿي وئي / ٽٽي ويو

sentences.native: سوري يار، مون کان تنهنجو فون ٽٽي ويو.
sentences.roman: sorī yār, moṃ khāṃ tunhinjo fon ṭuṭī vayo.
sentences.en: Sorry mate, I broke your phone (by accident).

sentences.native: مون کان وڏي غلطي ٿي وئي.
sentences.roman: moṃ khāṃ vaɗī ġalatī thī vaī.
sentences.en: I made a big mistake.

sentences.native: مون پنهنجي غلطي مڃي.
sentences.roman: moṃ panhinjī ġalatī mañī.
sentences.en: I admitted my mistake.

sentences.native: مون کي معاف ڪر، يار. منهنجو اهو مطلب نه هو.
sentences.roman: moṃ khe māf karu, yār. munhinjo uho matlabu na ho.
sentences.en: Forgive me, mate. I didn't mean it like that.

sentences.native: سائين، مون کي معاف ڪجو، دير ٿي وئي.
sentences.roman: sāīṃ, moṃ khe māf kajo, dera thī vaī.
sentences.en: I'm sorry I'm late, sir. (lit. forgive me, it got late)

sentences.native: هن مون کان معافي گهري.
sentences.roman: hun moṃ khāṃ māfī ghurī.
sentences.en: He apologised to me.

sentences.native: مون کان ڪالهه ڪم وسري ويو. سوري!
sentences.roman: moṃ khāṃ kālha kamu visirī vayo. sorī!
sentences.en: I completely forgot the job yesterday. Sorry!

sentences.native: هوءَ مون سان رسي پئي آهي.
sentences.roman: hūa moṃ sāṃ rusī paī āhe.
sentences.en: She's sulking with me.

sentences.native: هاڻي هن کي پرچائڻو پوندو.
sentences.roman: hāṇe hun khe parchāiṇo pavando.
sentences.en: Now I'll have to win her round.

sentences.native: ننڍي ڳالهه تي نه رس، يار.
sentences.roman: nanḍhī ɠālhi te na rusu, yār.
sentences.en: Don't sulk over a little thing, mate.

sentences.native: ڇا تون مون کي معاف ڪندين؟
sentences.roman: chhā tūṃ moṃ khe māf kandeṃ?
sentences.en: Will you forgive me?

tip.title: پهچڻ سان ئي · ڪندي · جيستائين
tip.body:
- **As soon as**: infinitive in -ṇa + **سان ئي**: گهر پهچڻ سان ئي فون ڪر.
- **While**: the -ndo stem ending in **-e**: کائيندي 'while eating'; doubled = 'in the middle of'.
- **Until**: **جيستائين** + a **negative**: جيستائين امان **نه** ايندي … 'until Mum comes'.

sentences.native: گهر پهچڻ سان ئي مون کي فون ڪر.
sentences.roman: ghara pahuchaṇa sāṃ ī moṃ khe fon karu.
sentences.en: Call me as soon as you get home.

sentences.native: هن کي ڏسڻ سان ئي مون کي کل اچي وئي.
sentences.roman: hun khe ɗisaṇa sāṃ ī moṃ khe khila achī vaī.
sentences.en: The moment I saw him I burst out laughing.

sentences.native: ماني کائيندي فون نه ڏس.
sentences.roman: mānī khāīnde fon na ɗisu.
sentences.en: Don't look at your phone while you're eating.

sentences.native: ڳالهائيندي ڳالهائيندي هو روئي پيو.
sentences.roman: ɠālhāīnde ɠālhāīnde hū roī peyo.
sentences.en: In the middle of talking he started crying.

sentences.native: جيستائين تون ٺيڪ نه ٿيندين، مان هتي رهندس.
sentences.roman: jestāīṃ tūṃ ṭhīku na thīndeṃ, māṃ hite rahandus.
sentences.en: I'll stay here until you're better. (man)

sentences.native: جيستائين امان نه ايندي، اسين ماني نه کائينداسين.
sentences.roman: jestāīṃ amāṃ na endī, asīṃ mānī na khāīndāsīṃ.
sentences.en: We won't eat until Mum gets here.

sentences.native: شام تائين مان آفيس ۾ آهيان.
sentences.roman: shāma tāīṃ māṃ āfīsa meṃ āhiyāṃ.
sentences.en: I'm at the office until the evening.

sentences.native: گهر پهچڻ سان ئي مون امان کي ڀاڪر پاتو.
sentences.roman: ghara pahuchaṇa sāṃ ī moṃ amāṃ khe bhākuru pāto.
sentences.en: As soon as I got home, I hugged Mum.

sentences.native: تو سان ڳالهائيندي دل کي سڪون ٿو ملي.
sentences.roman: to sāṃ ɠālhāīnde dila khe sukūnu tho mile.
sentences.en: Talking to you always calms me down.

sentences.native: ڪا ضرورت هجي ته ٻڌاءِ. مان ٻن منٽن ۾ پهچندس.
sentences.roman: kā zarūrata huje ta ɓudhāi. māṃ ɓin minaṭan meṃ pahuchandus.
sentences.en: If you need anything, tell me. I'll be there in two minutes. (man)

sentences.native: سوري؟ ڪا ڳالهه ناهي، ٿيندو آهي.
sentences.roman: sorī? kā ɠālhi nāhe, thīndo āhe.
sentences.en: Sorry? No worries, it happens.

lessons.title: Celebrating good news

tip.title: Congratulating someone
tip.body:
- **مبارڪون هجن!** = congratulations! On something: ترقيءَ **جون** مبارڪون (مبارڪون is f pl → جون).
- Proud of you: مون کي **تو تي** فخر آهي (polite: توهان تي).
- Good news means a treat: friends will say **مٺائي کاراءِ!** 'treat us to sweets!'

new: مون کي تو تي فخر آهي.

sentences.native: هڪ خوشخبري آهي! منهنجي ترقي ٿي وئي!
sentences.roman: hika xushxabarī āhe! munhinjī taraqī thī vaī!
sentences.en: I've got some good news! I got promoted!

sentences.native: واهه! مبارڪون هجن! دعوت ڪڏهن آهي؟
sentences.roman: vāh! mubārakūṃ hujan! daʿvata kaɗahiṃ āhe?
sentences.en: Wow, congratulations! When's the party?

sentences.native: منهنجو ڀاءُ امتحان ۾ پاس ٿي ويو!
sentences.roman: munhinjo bhāu imtihāna meṃ pāsu thī vayo!
sentences.en: My brother passed his exam!

sentences.native: امان کي تو تي ڏاڍو فخر آهي.
sentences.roman: amāṃ khe to te ɗāḍho faxru āhe.
sentences.en: Mum is so proud of you.

sentences.native: مون کي تو تي فخر آهي. تو ڏاڍي محنت ڪئي.
sentences.roman: moṃ khe to te faxru āhe. to ɗāḍhī mehnata kaī.
sentences.en: I'm proud of you. You worked really hard.

sentences.native: ترقيءَ جون مبارڪون هجن، سائين!
sentences.roman: taraqīa jūṃ mubārakūṃ hujan, sāīṃ!
sentences.en: Congratulations on your promotion, sir!

sentences.native: تنهنجي خوشخبري ٻڌي ڏاڍي خوشي ٿي.
sentences.roman: tunhinjī xushxabarī ɓudhī ɗāḍhī xushī thī.
sentences.en: I was so happy to hear your good news.

sentences.native: توهان جو پٽ پاس ٿيو؟ مبارڪون!
sentences.roman: tavhāṃ jo puṭu pāsu thiyo? mubārakūṃ!
sentences.en: Your son passed? Congratulations!

sentences.native: سچ پچ ساڙ ٿو ٿئي! مبارڪون هجن، يار.
sentences.roman: sach pach sāṛu tho thie! mubārakūṃ hujan, yār.
sentences.en: Honestly, I'm jealous! Congrats, mate.

tip.title: Condolences
tip.body:
- Say **اهو ٻڌي ڏاڍو ڏک ٿيو** 'I'm so sorry to hear it'.
- Muslims add **الله پاڪ مغفرت ڪري** (for the person who died) and **الله توهان کي صبر ڏئي** (for the family).
- Use the gentle **گذاري وڃڻ** 'pass away', in the plural for respect: ڏاڏا گذاري **ويا**.
- 'To go and pay condolences' = **پرسي لاءِ وڃڻ**.

sentences.native: منهنجا ڏاڏا گذاري ويا.
sentences.roman: munhinjā ɗāɗā guzārī vayā.
sentences.en: My grandfather has passed away. (respectful plural)

sentences.native: اهو ٻڌي ڏاڍو ڏک ٿيو، ادا. الله پاڪ مغفرت ڪري.
sentences.roman: uho ɓudhī ɗāḍho ɗukhu thiyo, adā. allāh pāku maġfirata kare.
sentences.en: I'm so sorry to hear it, brother. May God forgive him.

sentences.native: الله توهان کي صبر ڏئي، ادي.
sentences.roman: allāh tavhāṃ khe sabru ɗie, adī.
sentences.en: May God give you strength, sister.

sentences.native: اسين سڀاڻي پرسي لاءِ وينداسين.
sentences.roman: asīṃ subhāṇe purse lāi vendāsīṃ.
sentences.en: We'll go and pay our condolences tomorrow.

sentences.native: ڪالهه منهنجي دوست جي امان گذاري وئي.
sentences.roman: kālha munhinje dosta jī amāṃ guzārī vaī.
sentences.en: My friend's mother passed away yesterday.

sentences.native: ڏاڍو ڏک ٿيو. هو ڏاڍو سٺو ماڻهو هو.
sentences.roman: ɗāḍho ɗukhu thiyo. hū ɗāḍho suṭho māṇhū ho.
sentences.en: I'm so sorry. He was a really good man.

sentences.native: مون هن کي فون ڪري دلاسو ڏنو.
sentences.roman: moṃ hun khe fon karī dilāso ɗino.
sentences.en: I called him and comforted him.

sentences.native: گهڻا ماڻهو پرسي لاءِ آيا.
sentences.roman: ghaṇā māṇhū purse lāi āyā.
sentences.en: Lots of people came to pay their condolences.
